A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoDyn-Bench and contain readable main text, equations, Tables 1–9, Figures 1–5, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–D. Corresponding content can be matched despite relocation of the references.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of foundation models and geometric baselines, including benchmark results, threshold sensitivity, trajectory-encoding ablations, and temporal-resolution experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds an accuracy comparison between clips with rendering artifacts and the remaining simulated clips in Section 5.3.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, greedy balancing algorithm, deterministic oracle, trajectory encodings, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. The added pipeline attribution and release details do not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 1,000-clip benchmark, 14 question categories, and nuScenes, raw CARLA, and style-transferred CARLA domains. The new artifact analysis partitions existing simulated clips without adding data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The named comparators in the main and appendix experiments are unchanged. Section 4.2 replaces the example name DriveMM with RoboTron-Drive, which already appears in v1's Table 3. The new release description identifies no additional comparator results.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 adds a stratified evaluation comparing per-clip accuracy on 80 artifact-containing CARLA-transferred clips against the other 420. Existing benchmark sizes, frame sampling, metrics, and appendix protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a natural visual-artifact analysis testing whether rendering defects are associated with performance differences. The existing domain, threshold, parsing, encoding, and temporal-resolution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed aggregation, confidence intervals, or significance testing. V2 adds no uncertainty estimates or repeated-run information for the artifact comparison.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports artifacts in 80 of 500 simulated clips and accuracy differences of at most 3 percentage points versus the remaining 420, with mixed direction across leaderboard models. Existing tabulated results and plotted findings are unchanged; TartanVO's 67.78 to 67.8 is equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, consistency constraints, balancing equations, and baseline mappings are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow the claim that visual observations contribute negligible additional signal to negligible temporal signal. The benchmark contributions, perception-bottleneck claim, and benefits of explicit dynamics remain.

C2.justification: V2 newly attributes shuffle-invariant performance to downstream temporal integration rather than the visual encoder, argues against simple label forwarding, and interprets the artifact result as photometric insensitivity. The conclusion also explicitly limits coverage to short-horizon ego-motion, distinguishing it from long-horizon, multi-agent, and closed-loop evaluation.

D1.justification: Appendix D changes from an anonymous supplementary archive and promised release to a reported public, versioned release with code, dataset, and demo access information. It adds licenses, dataset contents and array dimensions, raw-output availability, and instructions for obtaining and joining nuScenes imagery. This substantially expands documented resource access; external availability was not verified.

R1.justification: V2 adds Gao et al.'s StyleVLA reference and attributes the simulation/curation pipeline to it in Section 3.2 and Appendix A.1. The remaining cited works and research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: V2 adds several short discussion and release passages, corrects the model-family example and appendix subsection references, and moves the bibliography before the appendices. Most prose and the scientific section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All five figures and nine tables retain their graphical content and structure. V2 corrects Table 5's caption typo and makes local placement and spacing changes as text and references reflow; the new artifact result is reported only in prose.

improvement.justification: V2 improves practical reproducibility through concrete release, licensing, and data-access instructions, and improves scope clarity through the temporal-signal qualification and explicit limitations. The artifact comparison adds limited supporting evidence. These gains are moderated by aggregate-only reporting of that comparison and stronger causal interpretations that the reported controls do not establish.
